title: False Signs and Wonders
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: False signs and wonders are supernatural or impressive works that deceive people and draw them away from God’s truth. Scripture warns believers not to judge spiritual truth by power displays alone.
summary: False signs and wonders are supernatural or impressive works that deceive people and draw them away from God’s truth. Scripture warns believers not to judge spiritual truth by power displays alone.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the truth and the true Lord of all power. Signs must never replace faithfulness to Him, His Gospel, and His Word.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture warns that not every sign is from God. Impressive works can deceive when they lead people away from the Lord, distort the truth, or serve rebellion.

Deuteronomy warns that even a sign that comes to pass must be rejected if it leads people after other gods. The truth of God’s Word is the standard above spiritual spectacle.

Jesus warned that false christs and false prophets would perform signs and wonders to deceive if possible. This means believers must be discerning, not gullible.

True faith is not built on chasing signs. God may work powerfully, but His people test all things by Scripture, the Gospel, and the lordship of Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People are often drawn to what feels powerful, dramatic, or supernatural. This can make them vulnerable to deception when spiritual experiences are not tested by truth.

This doctrine keeps believers anchored. Power without truth is dangerous. A sign that draws people away from Christ is not a reason for trust.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not measure truth by spectacle. Test every sign, claim, dream, prophecy, or spiritual experience by Scripture. If something weakens Christ, distorts the Gospel, excuses sin, or leads away from obedience, reject it no matter how impressive it appears.
